comment: Single source of truth for the radar look and behaviour, shared by the firmware (tools/gen_radar.mjs emits firmware/dragonradar/radar_assets.h) and the web preview (tools/preview/build.mjs embeds it). Lengths are fractions of the screen radius R (R = 233 px on the 466x466 panel), so every renderer draws the same picture at any size. Times are in milliseconds, colours are #RRGGBB. Screen coordinates: origin at the centre, x to the right, y down, bearings clockwise from north. See docs/design.md for the sources and the reasoning behind each value.

shading.comment: Screen fill: radial gradient screenCenter (at 0) -> screen (at midStop) -> screenEdge (at 1). A dark rim (theme.rim) of rimWidthR fades in towards the edge, where the green glass meets the casing. The sheen is a faint ellipse of glass reflection, upper left, as in the GT stills.

grid.comment: Square graticule fixed to the screen (it does not rotate with the heading, as in the anime). The centre of the screen sits in the middle of a cell (offsetCells 0.5), as in the Namek frames: about 9 cells across.

zoom.comment: The top button zooms out one level (the anime: each press shows more of the planet) and wraps from the widest back to the closest; the bottom one zooms in and wraps from the closest to the widest. The grid pitch stays the same on screen; what changes is the real distance per cell. View radius = cellM / pitchR.

marker.comment: The user: a red isosceles triangle with its centroid on the screen centre, apex pointing up (the heading, since the map is heading-up).

ball.comment: counts (per theme): stars = every dot carries the star number of its ball (1-7, unique); a group shows the stars of its nearest ball, next to its rightmost sphere; none = no digits. Dots closer than mergeR on screen form a group at their centroid, drawn as a little cluster of as many spheres as balls (as in the anime): 2 side by side, 3-6 on a ring (point up when odd, flat top when even), 7 a ring of six around one, with clusterSpacingR between neighbouring centres. Glow alpha at distance d from the centre: glowAlpha * b * (1 - d / glowR)^glowFalloff, where b is the blink brightness (dimLevel..1). The core is a solid disc coloured mix(ballDim, ballCore, b).

arrow.comment: Balls beyond visibleR are shown as a triangle on the edge, pointing outwards along their bearing (the wiki: the radar 'points arrows in the directions of nearby Dragon Balls'; drawn like the red edge marks of The Path to Power). Same blink as the balls. Arrows less than mergeDeg apart are drawn once.

blink.comment: All dots flash together on every radar beep: brightness rises to 1 in riseMs, then decays exponentially (time constant decayMs) towards dimLevel. With the beep off (muted or no ball) they pulse every periodMs.

scaleLabel.comment: Adaptation (not in the anime): after a zoom change the cell size shows for a moment under the marker, drawn with the stroke font.

zoom.comment: On a zoom change the old grid scales by the zoom ratio while fading out, the new one fades in, and the dots slide (log-interpolated scale) to their new positions.

powerOff.comment: Dots go first, then the whole screen fades to AMOLED black.

boot.comment: Power-on timeline from black. screen: fades in with two dim flickers; grid: lines revealed from the centre outwards; marker: blinks in; ping: one ring expands to the edge (adaptation, a single first scan, not a rotating sweep); balls: fade in, then the beep starts. The power_on sound starts at 0 and its two pips land on markerFromMs and pingFromMs.

sweep.comment: Scan effect, chosen by the user against the strict reading of the sources. mode: line = a hand that turns clockwise once every periodMs with a fading trail of trailDeg behind it (theme.sweep colour); dots flash as the hand crosses them when dotFlash is on. ring = a ring that grows from the centre to maxR over durationMs on every radar beep (syncToBeep). both = line and ring; none = no scan, only the beep blink. The preview offers the four so the user can pick one; mode is the default.

font.comment: Stroke font for the cluster counts and the scale label. Each glyph is a list of polylines on a 4 x 6 box (x right, y down); advance is the horizontal step per glyph, both in box units.

demo.comment: Seven sample balls for the preview and a firmware demo mode: bearing in degrees clockwise from north, distance in metres. Chosen so every zoom level shows something: at 10 m only ball 1 is on screen and the rest are edge arrows; at 100 m balls 1-3 show as separate dots; at 1 km balls 1-3 merge into a 3 and balls 5-6 into a 2; at 10 km balls 1-6 merge into a 6 at the centre and ball 7 appears.
